text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
* Two thousand tonnes of pears will be destroyed because there is no market for them due to the late summer and foreign competition.

* Paper pulp company Soporcel wants to press ahead with an investment in a new paper machine for 70 billion escudos, company president Alvaro Barreto said during a presentation about the company's six-month results.

* A decree on a new system of concessions for the motorways will be approved by the next cabinet. According to the plan, motorway users will no longer need to pay tolls which will be paid by the state.
* TAP pilots seek funds to participate in privatisation of state carrier TAP-Air Portugal.
* Maria dos Anjos Capote, director-general of the Treasury, said the state should not have conceded a guarantee for a 600 million escudo loan granted to union group UGT by state bank CGD.
* Construction companies Edifer and Engil signed a preliminary agreement in order to form a new economic group.
* The state will give financial support to a private group that will operate trains on the April 25 bridge over Lisbon.
